resources.string: Three cells hold only the same three digits between them; the rest of their unit can’t use them.
Three digits fit only the same three cells; those cells hold nothing else.
An X-Wing across three lines: a digit confined to three crossing lines clears the rest of them.
A cell with two candidates and two partners: whichever it is, one partner takes the third digit.
Three cells share just three digits between them.
Three digits share the same three cells.
One digit sits on only three crossing lines, across three lines.
A cell with two candidates sees two cells that each share one of them.
In %1$s, three cells can only be %2$d, %3$d or %4$d. They take all three, so no other cell there can.
The digits %2$d, %3$d and %4$d fit only the same three cells in %1$s, so those cells hold nothing else.

In %1$s, %2$s and %3$s, a %7$d fits only where they cross %4$s, %5$s and %6$s. Each line takes one of those spots, each in a different crossing line, so no other cell of %4$s, %5$s or %6$s can be %7$d.
The cell at %1$s can only be %4$d or %5$d. The cells at %2$s and %3$s each pair one of those with %6$d. Whichever it turns out to be, one of them is %6$d, so no cell that sees both can be %6$d.
